alignments.note: Portmanteau *wherein* spells the preposition into *-in* and the relative into *where-*, so both tokens take it as one aligned unit headed on the pronominal (rule 35).
Subject and the dummy *it* are inflection-licensed helpers (rules 7, 9); rule 17 heads the support-verb rendering on the meaning-bearing complement *strange*, not on *think*.

The supplied complementizer belongs to the non-finite complement the ASV expands into a finite clause (rule 85); *with them* realizes the participle's own συν- prefix and its supplied object, discontinuous under rule 15.
Subject of the genitive absolute, realized by *ye*.
The ASV gives *riot* no determiner, so the article has no *the* to anchor and the case preposition stays with the noun (rules 21, 23).
Source noun rendered *of + noun*; rule 17 heads it on the noun.

No Greek preposition governs 'of', so the phrasal frame and the supplied object are rule 7 helpers on the participle, as 'to rail at' is at 2PE.2.10. Rule 66 heads the unit on 'speaking': unlike 'think it strange' in this same verse, where 'think' glosses no part of xenizo and 'strange' renders the xen- root, 'speak' is itself the gloss of blasphemeo's -phem- and 'evil' only its generic modifier. The corpus heads blasphemeo on the verb word in all twelve of its units, TIT.3.2 'to speak evil of' on 'speak' unhedged, as katalalias -> 'evil speakings' heads on 'speakings' at 1PE.2.1.
